complexity_scope.guarantee: Per-instance expectation over X and Z; no high-probability guarantee.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Eq.(11) has explicit coefficients 2,1,1. Direction-law and dimension dependence enter s(d),M; L_P and M enter tuning and domain feasibility even though absent from the final expression.
complexity_scope.oracle: Two exact values of the same sampled function at θ_t and θ_t+u_tZ_t on the legal enlarged domain; exact Bregman minimization charged separately.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible arithmetic mean of θ_1,…,θ_k; expected objective gap to θ*.
complexity_scope.regime: Expanded Assumptions A–E and positive finite schedule parameters; C holds at u_1.
complexity_scope.resource: k rounds, k samples, 2k sample-function evaluations, k direction draws and k literal prox updates. No runtime, bit complexity or finite-precision bound.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected Algorithm alg.P027.smooth_md only; no lower bound or unrestricted Algorithm coverage.

map: p.13 Lemma 3 states Σ<g_t,θ_t−θ*>≤R²/[2α(k)]+(1/2)Σα(t)||g_t||_*². The source attributes this to [27, §2.3] and [7, Eq.(4.21)]; those external Proofs were not read.

p.14 Eq.(22) applies convexity and e_t=∇f(θ_t)−g_t. Lemma 1 bounds the conditional mean norm by u_tL_PM/2 and conditional second moment by 2s(d)G²+u_t²L_P²M²/2. A and strong convexity give ||θ_t−θ*||≤R.
p.14 Eq.(23) bounds the total expected gap by R²/[2α(k)]+s(d)G²Σα(t)+(L_P²M²/4)Σu_t²α(t)+(MRL_P/2)Σu_t.
The remaining p.14 displays use Σt^(-1/2)<2√k, Σt^(-5/2)≤4 and Σ1/t≤1+log k with the stated schedule. Jensen's inequality yields Eq.(11).

proofs.reading_coverage: Read and viewed the statement p.6 and all relevant §4.1 from Lemma 3 p.13 through the end of the Proof p.14; also read and viewed §4.2 p.15.

assumptions: Standing setting, p.2 Eq.(1): nonempty compact convex Θ⊂R^d; f finite on Θ; F(·;x) closed convex for P-almost every x; θ* a minimizer on Θ.
A, pp.3–4: differentiable ψ is 1-strongly convex with respect to ||·||, and Dψ(θ*,θ)≤R²/2 for every θ∈Θ.
B, p.4: measurable g(θ;x)∈∂F(θ;x), E g(θ;X)∈∂f(θ), and E||g(θ;X)||_*²≤G² for every θ∈Θ. In this smooth setting g=∇F and E g=∇f.
C, p.5 Eq.(7): dom F(·;x) contains Θ+u_1 supp μ for every x∈X; queried segments lie in the smooth domain.
Standing isotropy and D, pp.4–5: E ZZ^T=I_d, M=(E||Z||^4||Z||_*²)^(1/2)<∞, and E||<a,Z>Z||_*²≤s(d)||a||_*² for every a∈R^d.
E, p.5: for P-almost every x the sample gradient is L(x)-Lipschitz in the primal/dual norms, with L_P=(E L(X)²)^(1/2)<∞.
X_t iid from P; Z_t fresh from μ independently of X_t and previous draws. Both exact values share X_t. The Bregman minimization in Eq.(3) is solved exactly.
statement.objects_and_definitions: f(θ)=E F(θ;X), θ* minimizes f on Θ, and ||·||_* is dual to ||·||. Dψ(a,b)=ψ(a)−ψ(b)−<∇ψ(b),a−b>. For any θ_1∈Θ, set g_t=[F(θ_t+u_tZ_t;X_t)−F(θ_t;X_t)]Z_t/u_t and θ_(t+1)=argmin_{θ∈Θ}{<g_t,θ>+Dψ(θ,θ_t)/α(t)}. Output hatθ_k=(1/k)Σ_(t=1)^k θ_t.
statement.parameter_domains: Integers d,k≥1; R,G,L_P,M,s(d),α,u positive finite. For t≥1 choose α(t)=α R/[2G√s(d)√t] and u_t=u G√s(d)/[L_P M t]. This parametrized record excludes zero denominators. log denotes natural logarithm.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every instance satisfying the assumptions, any θ_1∈Θ and positive multipliers α,u whose u_1 satisfies C, the conclusion holds for every integer k≥1. Expectation is over all samples and directions.
